text.en: Kalela, a Kazdel mirror smith. Recommended by Rhodes Island's Kazdel Liaison Office personnel, she has reached a cooperative agreement with Rhodes Island to oversee the renovation and supply of mirrors for Rhodes Island dormitories. Prior to her return to Kazdel, she will also assist with Rhodes Island's forging operations.
text.zh: 卡莱朵，卡兹戴尔镜匠。经罗德岛驻卡兹戴尔办事处干员推荐，与罗德岛达成合作，负责罗德岛宿舍镜子的翻新及供应工作。在回到卡兹戴尔之前，也将协助进行罗德岛的锻造工作。

text.en:
Imaging tests show blurred organ outlines and abnormal shadows in the operator's thoracic cavity, with abnormal particulate counts in the circulatory system, indicating signs of Oripathy infection. The subject is confirmed at this stage as an Infected.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 10%
Operator Mirror Smith has a small amount of Originium crystals distributed on her body, specifically around her neck and upper arms, though her vocal cords remain undamaged.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.21 u/L
Having been exposed long-term to Kazdel's high-concentration Originium environment, Operator Mirror Smith's blood Originium-crystal density is relatively high. Following treatment, however, it is currently well-controlled.

During her physical examination, Operator Mirror Smith took a keen interest in the lenses installed on the testing equipment, leaning in to observe them directly while the apparatus was still running and emitting a strong glare. Fortunately, the Medical Department operator shut it down in time... otherwise, the damage caused to Mirror Smith's eyes by the bright light wouldn't be something a bottle of eye drops could fix.
"With such great light transmittance, how on earth was it polished?" Muttering to herself, Mirror Smith submitted a request to the Logistics Department for a set of lens samples to study.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓模糊，可见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测异常，有矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】10%
干员镜匠体表有少量源石结晶分布，具体分布于脖颈与上臂处，但并未对声带造成损伤。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.21u/L
长期暴露于卡兹戴尔的高浓度源石环境中，干员镜匠的血液源石结晶密度较高，目前经过治疗后，已得到较好控制。

体检时，干员镜匠对仪器上安装的透镜起了很大兴趣，甚至在仪器还在运作，发出强光时就直接偏头观察，还好医疗部干员及时将仪器关停……不然强光对镜匠眼睛造成的损伤，就不仅仅是现在这样开一瓶眼药水能解决的了。
“透光度这么好，它究竟是怎么打磨成的？”念叨着这些，镜匠向后勤部申请了一套透镜样品用来研究。

text.en:
Deciding to become a "mirror smith" was a difficult choice. The people of Kazdel had little demand for mirrors; "sometimes you'd run around the city all day and only sell two or three." Holding onto a try-it-and-see attitude, Kalela found the operator at Rhodes Island's Kazdel Liaison Office and asked if they needed any mirrors.
According to the liaison office operator, Kalela "pulled out four or five pocket mirrors like she was doing a magic trick, every single one featuring a beautifully patterned backing and a spotless glass surface." Yet when she asked about the price of the mirrors, the reply left her slightly taken aback.
"I was just... too anxious, too happy, and I had no idea what normal pricing was," Kalela explained afterward. Following a phone call between the liaison office operator and Closure, the partnership was quickly finalized, making Mirror Smith responsible for supplying mirrors throughout Rhodes Island.
"I didn't undercut anyone in a place like this... but her pricing is so 'generous' that it really does worry me. Once she goes back to Kazdel, how is she ever going to break even with prices like that?" Closure gazed at Kalela's back as she worked beside the furnace. "No way, I've got to talk to her!"

Over the next few days, under Closure's "tutorship," Kalela filled several pages with sales techniques, covering everything from pricing to pitching. The final evaluation involved Kalela re-quoting her prices, with Closure grading whether they were appropriate. Hearing Kalela quote a neither-too-high-nor-too-low price, Closure finally announced with satisfaction that the lessons were successfully concluded.
However, at the welcome party held for Kalela, she pulled out a bag of sparkling little trinkets as if performing another magic trick—she had gone ahead and fired a batch of tiny glass featherbeasts, scalebeasts, and cloudbeasts... all modeled after the new friends she had met at Rhodes Island.
"The feathers on my ears are solid-colored, but I actually have a white one! She even remembered that, and we'd only crossed paths once..." a Liberi operator excitedly explained to us, showing off the glass featherbeast in their hand, which genuinely possessed a trace of white on its forehead.
"Sigh... wasted lessons! Doesn't this mean she's losing money again?" Closure muttered to herself.

After all this, Mirror Smith gradually grew familiar with everyone at Rhodes Island. People started calling out to invite her to lunch at the cafeteria, or bringing her a small compact mirror to fix, exchanging their own stories for Mirror Smith's in the process. Perhaps she already viewed everyone at Rhodes Island as dear friends? Perhaps... whether she lost money or not was never something Mirror Smith truly cared about.
text.zh:
决定成为“镜匠”是一件困难的事。卡兹戴尔人对于镜子的需求量不高，“有时在城里跑一整天才卖出去两三面”。抱着试试看的心态，卡莱朵找到了罗德岛驻卡兹戴尔办事处的干员，询问这里是否需要镜子。
据办事处的干员所说，卡莱朵“像变戏法一般拿出四五面随身镜，个个背板都有漂亮的花纹，镜面也一尘不染”。而当她询问镜子的报价时，得到的回复却让她本人微微感到惊讶。
“我当时只是……太心急了，太开心了，也不知道正常的定价到底是多少。”事后，卡莱朵这样解释道。在办事处干员与可露希尔通过电话后，这项合作被迅速敲定，镜匠由此负责罗德岛上各处镜子的供应。
“我才没在这种地方压价……但她的定价太‘实惠’了，确实让我有些担心。回到卡兹戴尔之后，这种定价怎么能回本呢？”可露希尔望向在炉子旁工作的卡莱朵的背影，“不行，我得告诉她！”

后续几天，在可露希尔的“传授”下，卡莱朵记了好几页的售货技巧，从定价到推销一应俱全。而最后的成果验收环节，则是让卡莱朵自己重新报价，再由可露希尔来评定是否合适。当听到卡莱朵报出不高不低的定价后，可露希尔才满意地宣布这次授课圆满结束。
然而，在为卡莱朵举办的入职派对上，她却又像变戏法一样拿出一袋子亮晶晶的小东西——原来是她额外给大家烧的玻璃小羽兽、小鳞兽、小云兽……都是她基于在罗德岛遇到的这些新朋友的形象，烧制的一些小动物。
“我的耳羽看上去是纯色，但其实有一根白色的！她连这都记住了，可我们明明只有一面之缘……”一位黎博利干员激动地向我们解释，并展示手上的玻璃羽兽，其额头处真的有一道白色的痕迹。
“哎……白教了！这样不是又亏了嘛。”可露希尔嘟囔了一句。

这一切过后，镜匠和罗德岛的各位逐渐熟稔起来，开始有人喊着她一起去食堂吃饭，或拿来一面小化妆镜让她修补，顺便用自己的故事交换镜匠的故事。也许她已经把罗德岛的各位当成很好的朋友了？也许……亏不亏的，从来都不是让镜匠真正计较的事。

text.en:
Kalela found herself in a bit of a bind regarding the dormitory mirrors. Her work order stated clearly: renovate the Rhodes Island dormitory mirrors, duration two months, using the currently used mirrors as a standard. The mirrors currently used in the dormitories...? They had narrow white frames, identical dimensions, and looked entirely alike.
Yet, wouldn't making just one type of mirror be a little boring?
Perhaps driven by that very thought, she stayed by the furnace from morning till night. From glassblowing and plating to cutting and carving frames, the fire crackled continuously. In between blowing glass, Kalela would bring her notebook to the dormitories, painstakingly recording the names, races, and countries of origin of everyone living in each room.
The first mirror was completed in no time. Draped in a cloth, it was hung in a Sarkaz operator's dormitory. When the cloth was pulled away, the Sarkaz operator saw the mirror's wondrous design—unlike the uniform dormitory mirrors of the past, this was a circular mirror with a frame carved from black stone, featuring the horns of a "Sarkaz" and a tiny black tail.
The Sarkaz operator gasped in amazement, praising Kalela: "That's incredible, you even thought of this!" Kalela leaned against the doorframe with an embarrassed smile, and upon receiving this renewed affirmation, she hummed proudly—and thus, the news that she had crafted a "custom Sarkaz mirror" spread like wildfire, with everyone eager to see what the next mirror would look like.

"Hehe, look!" Zofia showed us a pocket mirror with a wooden-carved frame from which two Riftbeast ears "sprouted." The mirror behind Zofia was like an enlarged version of the small pocket mirror in her hand—with the difference that the larger mirror was crafted with greater detail, even engraving the names of Zofia and several other Ursus operators. "Pretty imposing, right? Kalela told me she carefully selected the wood color to match my hair color!"
Subsequently, the cloths draped over more mirrors were pulled away—"Cotas" mirrors with two long ears (Kalela even made a short-eared version for Sanya); an imposing "Adlivun" mirror adorned with iron plates...
Afterward, Kalela confessed that when she made the first mirror, her heart had been filled with anxiety. Back in Kazdel when she made mirrors, she was always told she was "wasting her time on useless things": pointless, unnecessary, a waste of effort... Would these "weird" custom frames receive the same dismissal?
The answer was self-evident.
Kalela smiled: "I still want to do these 'useless things.'"
text.zh:
卡莱朵对着宿舍镜子犯了难。她的工单上明明白白写着：翻新罗德岛宿舍镜子，工期两个月，以目前使用的镜子为标准即可。目前宿舍使用的镜子……？这种镜子拥有细白的镜框，尺寸相同，各个都长得一模一样。
可是，单做一种镜子是不是有点无聊？
也许正是抱着这样的念头，她才在炉子旁从早待到晚。从烧制玻璃到镀层，再到切割与雕刻镜框，炉火始终噼啪燃烧着，而在烧制玻璃的间隙，卡莱朵则拿着笔记本来到宿舍，一笔一划地记下每个宿舍里住着的人的名字、种族，和所属的国家。
第一面镜子很快就制作完成。它被蒙上了一层布，挂在一位萨卡兹干员的宿舍中。等揭开蒙着的布，萨卡兹干员才看见那面镜子的奇妙之处——不同于之前统一的宿舍镜子，这是一面圆镜，镜框则用黑色岩石雕刻而成，上面还有着“萨卡兹”的角，以及一条小小的黑色尾巴。
这位萨卡兹干员惊呼一声，夸卡莱朵：“太厉害了，这都能想到！”而卡莱朵则倚在门框上不好意思地笑笑，再次得到肯定后，她骄傲地哼哼两声——于是，她做出了一面“萨卡兹定制镜子”的事火速流传开来，大家都在期待着下一面镜子会做成什么样。

“嘿嘿，你看！”烈夏向我们展示了一面随身镜，有着木头雕刻的镜框，镜框上“长着”两只裂兽耳朵。而烈夏身后的那面镜子就像她手中这面小随身镜的放大版——不一样的是，大镜子做得更加精细，上面甚至还刻了烈夏和另外几位乌萨斯干员的名字。“很威风吧？卡莱朵跟我说，镜框木头的颜色是她精挑细选过的，和我的发色很像呢！”
随后，更多面镜子上盖着的布被揭下来——有两个长耳朵的“卡特斯”镜（卡莱朵甚至给珊比做了短耳朵版本）；威风凛凛、装饰着铁片的“阿达克利斯”镜……
事后，卡莱朵坦陈，她在做出第一面镜子的时候心情其实很忐忑。在卡兹戴尔做镜子时，她总得到“瞎忙活”的评价：没用、不需要、白费力气……这次“奇怪的”定制镜框，是否也会得到一样的评价？
答案显而易见。
卡莱朵笑了起来：“我还是想做这些‘没有用的事’。”

text.en:
After renovating all the mirrors in the Rhodes Island dormitories, Kalela saved up enough money and prepared to return to Kazdel to officially open a mirror shop. Before setting off, however, she received a letter.
[A Letter from Kazdel]
Our dear daughter,
How are you? It's been about three months since you left Kazdel to go into business. How is business going, have your mirrors sold? Although your mother and I used to disapprove of your mirror business, but... now that the war has been over for so long, we are learning to slowly accept some changes.
Take your father's weapon shop, for instance. Fewer and fewer people are coming to buy the blades and swords he forges. Occasionally someone comes by with tools, but it's just to have him do repairs, or simply to sharpen their kitchen knives... otherwise they can't even chop potatoes. Business hasn't been great, and he used to sit there all day sighing over the swords and blades he'd forged. You had advised him to turn the weapon shop into a smithy and forge iron bed frames and tables for everyone... Back when you first left he couldn't accept the change, but after feeling glum for a long time, it seems your father took those words to heart—just the other day he took an order for a bed frame, and right now he's probably hammering away right beside the stove at home.
Mother is rambling. We still have that mirror you left behind at home—lately, some people have come looking for Mother, asking where you went because they want to buy mirrors. Mother thought she knew a bit of forging craft herself, so she tried blowing some glass, but whatever she made always turned out cloudy, not nearly as pretty as yours. So Mother wanted to write and ask you, what are the raw materials for mirrors, and what are the proportions?
Note: This letter was written on behalf by someone else, please excuse any omissions.
With love, Mother

Upon receiving this letter, Kalela immediately found operators familiar with the Sarkaz language and asked them to help draft a reply. She read out her words sentence by sentence, stumbling and halting, wanting to convey her thoughts yet always feeling them tangle at the tip of her tongue, unable to sort them out. When she reached the raw material ratios for glass, she had no idea how to translate them into writing, let alone whether her proportions would work in the old, pitch-black forging stove back home.
So she apologetically nodded to the operator holding the pen, took the remaining half-written letter, jotted down a few phrases, and ultimately crossed them all out, leaving just five large characters and two exclamation marks—"I'm coming right back!!"
This "half-letter" was naturally mailed out at once, and Kalela departed at the same time toward their shared destination—and we trust that Kalela will arrive ahead of this letter, carrying the formula, her yearning, and the blueprint for Kazdel's first mirror shop...
text.zh:
把罗德岛宿舍的镜子全部翻新后，卡莱朵攒够了钱，准备回到卡兹戴尔，正式开一间镜子铺。但她在动身前，却收到了一封信。
【一封来自卡兹戴尔的信】
我们的女儿：
你好吗？距离你离开卡兹戴尔去做生意已经差不多三个月了。生意做得如何，你的镜子卖出去了吗？虽然爸爸妈妈曾经不赞成你的镜子生意，但……战争过去这么久，我们也正学着慢慢接受一些改变。
就拿你爸爸的武器铺举例，买他锻的刀、剑的人变得越来越少了。偶尔有人拿着刀具过来，都是让他做修补的工作，或者干脆只是让他把菜刀磨利……否则就连土豆都切不碎了。生意没那么好，他之前也成天对着自己锻的那些刀和剑叹气。你劝过他，把武器铺改成铁匠铺，为大家打一些铁床架、铁桌子……虽然你刚走那阵子他还无法接受这改变，但在郁闷很久之后，你爸爸似乎也听进去了这些话——这几天他刚接了个床架的单子，现在应该就在家里的炉子旁边敲敲打打呢。
妈妈说远了。家里还留着你之前放着的一面镜子——这几天，有些人来找妈妈，问你去哪了，他们想买镜子。妈妈想，自己也会点锻造的手艺，于是就试着烧了烧，但烧出来的东西总是浑浊，不如你做的漂亮。所以妈妈想写信问问你，镜子的原料是什么，配比又是如何？
注：这封信由他人代写，如有文字遗漏还请见谅。
爱你的妈妈

收到这封信后，卡莱朵立刻找到熟悉萨卡兹语的干员，请他们帮忙代写一封回信。她一字一句地念着，磕磕绊绊，想传达自己的话，却总觉得那些话在嘴边绕着，捋不清楚。等她念到玻璃的原料配比时，更不知道怎样把它说成字句，自己的配比又是否适用于家里那个黑漆漆的、用了许久的锻造炉。
于是，她不好意思地向写着字的干员点点头，自己拿着那剩下半封没写的信，写了几句话，最终还是全部划掉，留下了大大的五个字和两个感叹号——“我马上回去！！”
这“半封”信当然在第一时间就寄出，卡莱朵也和这封信同时出发，朝着共同的目的地——而我们相信，卡莱朵会带着配方、思念，以及卡兹戴尔第一间镜子铺的雏形……比这封信更先到达。

text.en:
[An Audio Log, from the Rhodes Island Kazdel Liaison Office]
"She asked me this very question when she first found the Rhodes Island office in Kazdel. You could tell she wasn't very confident about her own question—and I found out later that she had already asked many, many people the same thing, without getting an answer."
"She asked me if I knew of a place in Kazdel, long before the war even began, that was clean, tidy, and had a spacious, bright hall. She smiled sheepishly, saying she had met a Caprinae lady there and seen a mirror for the first time. It was because of this encounter with that Caprinae that she realized, long afterward, perhaps Kazdel didn't need so many weapons anymore, but rather a mirror."
"But unfortunately, I could only deduce that the place she described might be the predecessor of Rhodes Island, yet I was helpless against her next question: 'Is that Caprinae still around? How is she doing now?'"
"...I don't know. To be honest, I feel pessimistic about that question... but surely after coming to Rhodes Island, she might seek out some answers?"

[An Audio Log, from Operator Odall]
"I can't be certain that the Caprinae she's looking for is... my mother. I only have some childhood impressions of my mother, and they're a bit hazy. But Kalela could clearly describe the appearance of the Caprinae she remembered, even down to details like how many loops her horns had."
"Yet as we continued talking, both she and I realized there was an inescapable answer to her question—too few people like her parents had survived the war. We both knew it in our hearts."
"You're asking about Kalela? After the conversation ended, she fell silent and then left."

[A Transcript of a Conversation]
"I just held onto a shred of fantasy, wondering if she might have a chance to see today's Kazdel—a Kazdel with me in it now. Knowing that the house I saw in my childhood was the predecessor of Rhodes Island is already enough for me. And everything I've seen on Rhodes Island proves that there are still countless people persisting in what they ought to persist in."
"Feeling disappointed or defeated? Why would you ask such a question?"
"..."
"As for mirrors, of course I'm going to keep making them. I'll go back to Kazdel—it's waiting for me... There are still many things waiting for me to do and see there."
text.zh:
【某段语音记录，来自罗德岛驻卡兹戴尔办事处】
“她在卡兹戴尔，找到罗德岛办事处的时候，就曾经问过我这个问题。你能看出来她对自己的问题并不自信——后来我才知道，她已经问过很多、很多人这个问题了，但都没有得到答案。”
“她问我知不知道，早在战争还没开始时，卡兹戴尔曾经有一个地方，干净整洁，拥有宽敞明亮的大厅。她不好意思地笑了笑，说自己曾在那里遇到一位卡普里尼女士，也第一次见到镜子。正是因为和卡普里尼的这次相遇，她才在很久之后意识到，也许卡兹戴尔不再需要那么多的武器，而是需要一面镜子。”
“但很遗憾，我只能推测出她所描述的那个地方可能是罗德岛的前身，却对她的下一个问题无能为力：‘那位卡普里尼还在吗？她现在过得怎么样？’”
“……我不知道。说实话，我对这个问题感到悲观……但想必她来到罗德岛后，能够寻求到一些答案？”

【某段语音记录，来自干员奥达】
“我没办法确定她想找的那名卡普里尼就是……我母亲。对母亲，我只有一些小时候的印象，已经有点模糊。但卡莱朵却能清晰地讲出她记得的那名卡普里尼的容貌，甚至还有类似于角弯了几个圈的细节。”
“但随着我们继续说下去，我和她都能意识到，她的问题只有一个无可避免的答案——像她父母那样能够在战争中存活下来的人太少太少了。对这件事，我们都心知肚明。”
“你问卡莱朵？结束对话后，她陷入了沉默，然后离开了。”

【某段对谈记录】
“我只是抱有一丝幻想，想着她是否有机会能够看见如今的卡兹戴尔——有现在的我的，卡兹戴尔。能够得知童年时见到的那栋房子就是罗德岛的前身，这对我来讲已经够好了。而我在罗德岛上见到的一切，也证明了还有许许多多的人在坚持着应该坚持的事。”
“感到失望，或是挫败？你为什么会问这样的问题？”
“……”
“至于镜子，我当然还会一直做下去。我会回到卡兹戴尔——它在等我……那里还有许多等着我去做、去看的事。”

text.en:
[Words previously unsaid, retained in writing through consultation between Kalela and the HR Department]
To the unknown Caprinae lady:
Hello! I've decided to open a new shop, specializing in mirrors, right here in Kazdel. Just thinking about it gets me a bit excited; this might just be Kazdel's very first mirror shop. Just like before I decided to make mirrors, I went to the tailor to order a new dress—only this time, there are many more beautiful clothes already made and waiting to be picked up in the tailor's shop. That means things are getting better here, right?
To be honest, there were many moments when I wanted to give up, and indeed I did give up. At its worst, the furnace went unlit for three days. No one thought what I made was useful, so why keep going? But... I thought about hammering away at home in the weapon shop... Was I really going to go back to hammering away, now that the war was over?
So I lit the furnace again, trying to find an opportunity—and finally secured the order from Rhodes Island. I used that money to return to Kazdel and made the decision I just told you about.
Fortunately, I now understand what I ought to be doing. Though sometimes I still worry about all sorts of messy little trifles. I plan to hire an apprentice these days, but will anyone be willing to come? Still, even if it's just me... this time I won't let the furnace go cold again.
text.zh:
【一段曾经并未说出口的话，经卡莱朵与人事部协商后作书面留存】
致不知名的卡普里尼女士：
你好！我决定开一家新店铺，专门卖镜子，在卡兹戴尔。想想还有些激动，这可能是卡兹戴尔第一间镜子铺呢。就像决定做镜子前一样，我又去找裁缝定了一身新的裙装，只不过这次，裁缝铺里已售未取的漂亮衣服比之前要多许多。这也意味着，这里在慢慢变好，对吗？
实话说，我也有许多想要放弃的时刻，甚至真的放弃过。最严重的时候，炉子冷了三天没烧火。没人觉得我做的东西有用，那为什么要继续呢？可是……我想到之前，在家里的武器铺敲敲打打……难道我还要回去敲敲打打吗，在战争已经结束的现在？
所以我还是把炉子烧起来了，努力找机会——终于找到了罗德岛的订单。我拿着这笔钱回到了卡兹戴尔，做出了我刚才和你说的那个决定。
所幸如今，我明白了自己应该做的事。虽然有时候还是会担心许多乱七八糟的小事。这几天我打算招个学徒，可有没有人愿意过来呢？不过，就算只有我一个人……这次我也不会再让炉子冷下来了。
